SEA.head: A slightly uphill night for the Kraken
SEA.body: Even though Seattle has home-ice advantage, the Rangers have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Seattle will be without McCann. The Kraken’s best way to tip it is keeping dangerous shots away.

NYR.head: Leaning the Rangers’ way

story.head: Tolvanen returns to Seattle
paras: The Kraken (8-5-1) lost 6-2 to Calgary on Oct 30, and the Rangers are on a three-game losing streak. Going in, the Rangers are fifth in the Metropolitan (tied for 19th in the NHL) and the Kraken third in the Pacific (tied for 13th).
The Rangers’ record (.536) is about what their chances are worth. The Kraken’s record (.607) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.442), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Rangers lean on their stars as much as almost anyone (2nd lowest), forecheck as hard as almost anyone (2nd) and get a lot of their shots blocked (32nd). As for the Kraken, they rarely threaten on the penalty kill (32nd) and give up a lot of shots (32nd). They also roll their lines more evenly than almost anyone (2nd), so the Kraken roll four lines, but the Rangers lean on their top six. The Rangers’ power play (8th) could do real damage against the Kraken’s penalty kill (31st).

Adam Fox (1 G / 16 A / 17 P in 14 GP) leads the Rangers in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Alexis Lafrenière (9 G / 7 A / 16 P in 14 GP) has a team-high nine goals. For the Kraken, Chandler Stephenson (2 G / 10 A / 12 P in 14 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Frédérick Gaudreau (7 G / 3 A / 10 P in 14 GP) has a team-high seven goals.
Dylan Garand (4-5-1 / .899 SV% in 8 GS) will likely start for the Rangers, and Philipp Grubauer (5-2-1 / .886 SV% in 8 GS) for Seattle.
At home, Lane Lambert likes to send Winterton, Meyers and Douglas out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Tolvanen, Glendening and Raddysh.

items.text: Eeli Tolvanen faces Seattle for the first time since leaving.
The Rangers are newly without Sean Durzi, and have had to make do without Matthew Robertson and Scott Morrow all season.
The Kraken are newly without Jared McCann.
Mackie Samoskevich has six goals on chances worth about 2.1 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
